newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on exporters' activity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on exporters' activity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended higher against its American counterpart on Wednesday on continued U.S. dollar selling by local exporters, dealers said.
The local dollar finished at T$27.489 against Tuesday's T$27.493 close. Turnover through dealers was a modest T$140.5 million.
"U.S. dollar sales are expected to continue before the Chinese lunar new year (on February 7), but the central bank is likely to smooth any sharp movements," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The softness of the U.S. dollar overseas also helped strengthen local currency, dealers said.

The said that Taiwan stock-index futures being launched by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore International Monetary Exchange on Thursday may lure more inflows of foreign equity funds for the island's bourse. But the planned launches had no immediate impact on the local foreign exchange market.
"If the local stock market remains bullish, we can expect more inflows of foreign equity funds," the dealer said.
Taiwan's stock index surged 144.41 points or 2.10 percent higher to a two-year high of 7,019.43 points.
A steady T$27.48-49 range was seen for Thursday.
